gloss: plunge pool; basin at the foot of a waterfall

definitions.gloss: plunge pool; basin at the foot of a waterfall
definitions.explanation: The deep pool of water formed at the base of a waterfall by the force of the falling water. A natural feature found at many famous waterfalls.

examples.japanese: {滝壺|たきつぼ}の{水|みず}は{冷|つめ}たかった。
examples.english: The water in the plunge pool was cold.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{滝壺|たきつぼ}で{泳|およ}いでいる。
examples.english: The children are swimming in the plunge pool.

examples.japanese: {遊歩道|ゆうほどう}を{下|くだ}っていくと、{滝壺|たきつぼ}のすぐそばまで{近|ちか}づくことができ、{水|みず}しぶきが{顔|かお}にかかる。
examples.english: If you walk down the trail, you can get right up close to the plunge pool, and the spray hits your face.

notes:
Composed of {滝|たき} (waterfall) and {壺|つぼ} (pot, basin). The metaphor of a pot captures the round, deep shape of the pool carved out by falling water.

USAGE:
Frequently encountered in nature tourism, hiking guides, and descriptions of scenic spots. Japan has many famous waterfalls ({名瀑|めいばく}), and the {滝壺|たきつぼ} is often highlighted as a destination point on hiking trails. Some {滝壺|たきつぼ} are deep enough for swimming in summer, while others are used for {滝行|たきぎょう} (waterfall meditation practice).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {滝壺|たきつぼ}に{落|お}ちる: to fall into the plunge pool
- {滝壺|たきつぼ}で{泳|およ}ぐ: to swim in the plunge pool
- {滝壺|たきつぼ}の{深|ふか}さ: depth of the plunge pool
- {滝壺|たきつぼ}まで{下|お}りる: to descend to the plunge pool

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {滝|たき}: waterfall — the waterfall itself; {滝壺|たきつぼ} is specifically the pool at its base
- {淵|ふち}: deep pool (in a river) — a general term for a deep, still section of a river, not necessarily at the base of a waterfall
- {渓流|けいりゅう}: mountain stream — the flowing water in a valley or gorge
